title: test_decode_phase3b0 host heap corruption / SIGSEGV — Linux root cause
summary: The historically 'one-time, never reproduced' test_decode_phase3b0 heap-corruption exit is deterministic on Linux: 20/20 in both the Release and ASan/UBSan builds, and the full Linux CUDA CTest fails only this test (SegFault). Root cause is an upstream encoder unsupported-format path, not a Phase 3B-2A decoder defect.

environment.compiler: GCC 14.2.0 (Debug), nvcc host GCC 13.3.0 (CUDA ASan build)

root_cause.explanation: CSampleEncoder::PrepareToEncode reaches assert(0) for the RG24->RGBA_4444 conversion because no Toggle444vs422 / Toggle4444vs444 / Toggle4444vs422 route yields the requested encoded format. With asserts active (Debug/ASan) it aborts cleanly; in Release (NDEBUG, used by CI and releases) the assert is compiled out and the encoder runs in an inconsistent state and SIGSEGVs during CFHD_EncodeSample.
root_cause.why_it_looked_like_a_flake: Release-mode undefined state can surface as a heap-corruption abort or a clean fault depending on allocator/heap layout; an assert-active run never reaches the undefined state.

unsupported_conversions_measured.method: assert-active (ASan Debug) build; 'Assertion 0 failed' at SampleEncoder.cpp:260 means the pair is unsupported

not_claimed: not a FIELDPLUS / Phase 3B-2A decoder defect (crash is in the upstream encoder path)
not proven to be the exact single Windows observation; it establishes the class reproducibly

the ASan heap-buffer-overflow at upstream/Codec/spatial.c:537 (FilterHorizontalRow16s) is an internal upstream SIMD over-read on the supported YUV path, separate from this crash and out of scope (upstream is frozen)
suggested_follow_up: test_decode_phase3b0 should skip/record every unsupported input->encoded pair (extend the existing deny-list with the table above) so a Release build cannot crash on an unimplemented SDK conversion
upstream assert(0) guards for user-reachable parameter combinations should return CFHD_ERROR_* instead; requires a maintainer decision because it touches upstream/ (rule 1)
